page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable instance belonging to the ecs.t6 family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 2 vCPUs, 1.0 thread per core, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and its baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.t6-c1m4.large operates in the lower performance tiers. Its stress-ng single-core score of 1161.28 and multi-core score of 2371.48 are categorized as weak, falling in the bottom 25 percent. Memory performance is also constrained, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 22.38 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score of 1168.91, both falling into the bottom 10 percent category. The burstable CPU allocation model means that sustained high-compute workloads will deplete CPU credits, leading to throttled performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is designed as a budget-friendly option for workloads with low baseline resource utilization that experience occasional activity spikes. Due to its poor performance in database operations with a Passmark database score of 701.22 and static web serving at 2.58 GB/sec, it is unsuitable for high-traffic production environments. Appropriate workloads include low-traffic web servers, development or testing environments, code repositories, and simple background tasks that do not require continuous high CPU or memory throughput.
